author: BlackEmpire
message: Në këtë ditë të shenjtë dhe të bekuar, uroj që zemrat tuaja të mbushen me paqe, dashuri dhe mirësi. Kurban Bajrami është një kujtesë e madhe e sakrificës, besimit dhe përkushtimit ndaj Zotit, por edhe e solidaritetit me njëri-tjetrin, duke ndarë me ata që kanë nevojë dhe duke forcuar lidhjet familjare e shoqërore. Le të jetë kjo festë një fillim i ri për më shumë mirëkuptim, falje dhe harmoni në jetën tuaj. Uroj që çdo shtëpi të mbushet me gëzim, çdo zemër të lehtësohet nga shqetësimet dhe çdo hap i juaji të jetë i bekuar dhe i udhëzuar në rrugën e drejtë. Mos harrojmë në këtë ditë të rëndësishme të kujtojmë ata që nuk janë më me ne, të ndihmojmë të varfrit dhe të tregojmë dashuri ndaj familjes, fqinjëve dhe miqve. Sepse vlera e vërtetë e Kurban Bajramit nuk është vetëm në festim, por në veprat e mira që bëjmë dhe në zemrën e pastër me të cilën i bëjmë ato. Uroj që Zoti t’ju pranojë lutjet, kurbanet dhe çdo vepër të mirë që keni bërë. Paçi shëndet, lumturi dhe begati në jetën tuaj sot dhe gjithmonë. Gëzuar Kurban Bajramin!

author: 𝓚𝓵𝓮𝓪𓆩♡𓆪
message: Smoking is one of the few habits that harms nearly every part of the human body at the same time. It affects the lungs, heart, brain, skin, teeth, blood vessels, immune system, mental health, fitness, sleep, and even the lives of people nearby. Millions of people around the world smoke because nicotine is addictive, because of stress, social pressure, habit, curiosity, or advertising influence. But when you look at the full picture — physically, mentally, financially, and socially — smoking creates far more damage than most people realize at first. The biggest reason people should not smoke is simple: it destroys health slowly and continuously. Cigarette smoke contains thousands of chemicals, including toxic substances and cancer-causing compounds. Every puff sends harmful particles into the lungs and bloodstream. Over time, these chemicals damage tissue and reduce the body’s ability to repair itself. Unlike injuries that happen suddenly, smoking causes gradual damage day after day, year after year. That slow damage is dangerous because people often do not notice how serious it has become until the consequences are severe. One of the most obvious effects of smoking is lung damage. The lungs are designed to bring oxygen into the body, but smoke coats them with tar and toxins. Tiny air sacs called alveoli begin to break down, making breathing harder. Smokers often develop chronic coughing, wheezing, shortness of breath, and reduced stamina. Simple activities like climbing stairs, running, or even walking long distances can become exhausting. Over time, smoking can lead to diseases such as chronic bronchitis and emphysema, which are forms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, also called COPD. People with severe COPD may eventually need oxygen tanks just to breathe comfortably. Smoking is also one of the leading causes of lung cancer. Cancer develops when damaged cells grow uncontrollably. Tobacco smoke repeatedly injures lung cells, increasing the chance that dangerous mutations form. Lung cancer is especially deadly because it is often discovered late. Many smokers underestimate their own risk because they assume cancer only happens to “heavy smokers” or older people, but damage begins almost immediately after regular smoking starts. The heart and blood vessels are also heavily affected. Smoking narrows blood vessels and raises blood pressure. It makes the heart work harder while reducing the amount of oxygen available in the blood. This increases the risk of heart attacks, strokes, and circulation problems. Some smokers develop poor blood flow to the legs and feet, which can lead to chronic pain or even tissue damage. The cardiovascular system depends on healthy circulation, and smoking weakens it constantly. Another major issue is addiction. Nicotine changes the brain’s reward system. At first, smoking may seem relaxing or enjoyable, but over time the brain begins depending on nicotine to feel normal. This creates cravings, irritability, anxiety, and withdrawal symptoms when a person tries to stop. Many smokers do not actually enjoy every cigarette; instead, they smoke to temporarily remove the discomfort caused by nicotine withdrawal. Addiction traps people into repeating the habit even when they know it is harming them. Smoking also affects appearance and aging. It reduces blood flow to the skin, which decreases oxygen and nutrients reaching skin cells. Smokers often develop wrinkles earlier than non-smokers, and skin can appear dull or dry. Teeth become stained, breath smells unpleasant, and fingers may yellow from tobacco exposure. Hair can also become weaker and thinner. While appearance may seem less important than health, many people underestimate how strongly smoking changes the body externally over time. Another reason not to smoke is the financial cost. Cigarettes are expensive, especially over many years. A person smoking one pack a day can spend thousands annually. Over a decade, that money could have gone toward travel, education, hobbies, savings, emergencies, or major life goals. Many smokers are shocked when they calculate how much they have spent across years of addiction. The tobacco industry profits massively while consumers pay financially and physically. Smoking also harms people nearby through secondhand smoke. Family members, friends, coworkers, and children can inhale the same toxic chemicals without choosing to smoke themselves. Secondhand smoke increases risks of lung disease, heart disease, asthma attacks, and cancer in non-smokers. Children exposed to smoke may develop breathing problems, ear infections, and increased health complications. Pregnant women exposed to smoke may face additional risks affecting both mother and baby. This means smoking is not only a personal health issue — it can affect entire households and communities. The effects on fitness and athletic performance are also significant. Smoking reduces oxygen delivery and lung efficiency, which lowers endurance and slows recovery after exercise. Athletes who smoke usually struggle more with stamina and breathing compared to non-smokers. Even people who are not athletes may notice fatigue, reduced energy, and slower healing from injuries or illness. Many people believe smoking helps reduce stress, but this is misleading. Nicotine addiction creates cycles of tension and relief. A smoker feels stressed partly because nicotine levels drop, then temporarily feels calmer after smoking again. In reality, smoking often increases baseline stress and anxiety over time. Studies frequently show that many former smokers report feeling less stressed after quitting permanently. Without nicotine dependence controlling the brain’s reward system, emotional stability can improve. Smoking can also reduce quality of life in ways people do not expect. Constant smoke breaks interrupt activities. Long flights, events, or workdays may become uncomfortable because of cravings. Clothes, cars, and homes may smell like smoke. Some social environments discourage smoking entirely. Relationships can be affected when loved ones worry about health risks or dislike exposure to smoke. Over time, the habit can control daily routines more than people realize. The tobacco industry’s history is another important reason to avoid smoking. For decades, major tobacco companies knew cigarettes were addictive and harmful, yet advertising often portrayed smoking as glamorous, sophisticated, rebellious, or relaxing. Marketing campaigns targeted young people aggressively because addiction is easier to establish early in life. Understanding this history helps explain why smoking became so widespread despite overwhelming health risks. Quitting smoking is difficult, but the human body begins recovering surprisingly quickly after stopping. Within hours, heart rate and blood pressure improve. Within days, carbon monoxide levels decrease. Over weeks and months, breathing and circulation often improve. Over years, the risk of serious disease drops significantly compared to continued smoking. The body has remarkable healing abilities when exposure to smoke ends. There are also broader societal costs. Healthcare systems spend enormous amounts treating smoking-related diseases. Lost productivity, medical expenses, and preventable deaths create economic strain worldwide. Smoking-related illnesses affect families emotionally and financially. Loved ones may spend years caring for relatives suffering from cancer, heart disease, or respiratory failure caused by tobacco use. Some people argue that smoking is a personal choice, and in one sense that is true. Adults can make decisions about their own bodies. However, truly informed choices require understanding the full consequences. Many smokers begin when they are very young, before fully understanding addiction or long-term health effects. Nicotine dependence can form quickly, making later “choice” much more complicated. There is also the issue of environmental impact. Cigarette butts are among the most common forms of litter worldwide. They contain toxic chemicals that can pollute water and soil. Tobacco production also uses land, water, pesticides, and industrial processes that affect ecosystems. Smoking therefore has environmental consequences in addition to human health effects. One of the saddest realities about smoking is that many smokers wish they had never started. Former smokers often describe how difficult quitting became and how strongly addiction controlled their behavior. Many people begin casually, thinking they can stop anytime. But nicotine dependence grows gradually until quitting feels extremely challenging. Young people especially should avoid smoking because the teenage brain is more vulnerable to addiction. Habits formed early can last decades. Starting smoking at a young age dramatically increases the likelihood of long-term dependence and health complications later in life. What begins as experimentation can become a lifelong struggle. In modern society, there are far healthier ways to manage stress, socialize, or relax. Exercise, hobbies, friendships, music, therapy, meditation, sports, creative activities, and healthy routines provide benefits without destroying the body. Smoking may offer short-term stimulation or comfort, but the long-term costs are enormous compared to the temporary effects. Ultimately, people should not smoke because the risks touch nearly every aspect of life. Smoking damages health, shortens lifespan, drains money, weakens physical fitness, harms appearance, affects loved ones, increases disease risk, and creates addiction that is difficult to escape. While quitting can be challenging, avoiding smoking in the first place is one of the best decisions a person can make for their future health and quality of life.

message: Ai nuk është i dënuar dhe nuk akuzohet zyrtarisht për vepra penale. Në diskutimet publike në Shqipëri, emri i Agron Shehajt lidhet me konceptin e "krimeve" në dy kontekste të tjera plotësisht ligjore dhe politike: 1. Denoncimi i krimeve të komunizmit Agron Shehaj është një nga zërat më aktivë në politikën shqiptare për dënimin e krimeve të periudhës komuniste. Ai është themelues i Fondacionit Kujto, një arkivë online që dokumenton krimet e komunizmit, viktimat e diktaturës, të pushkatuarit dhe të burgosurit politikë në Shqipëri. Dekomunistizimi: Përmes debateve publike dhe nismave, ai ka kërkuar hapjen e plotë të dosjeve të ish-Sigurimit të Shtetit dhe largimin e ish-zyrtarëve komunistë nga postet 2. Denoncimi i skandaleve korruptive Si deputet i Kuvendit të Shqipërisë dhe lider i partisë "Mundësia", Shehaj ka denoncuar shpesh në publik dhe në SPAK raste që ai i quan "krime ekonomike" ose korrupsion qeveritar: 1 Skandalin e inceneratorëve. Procedurat e dyshimta të tenderave publikë. Çështjet e pronave dhe investitorëve strategjikë.
